business_summary: GE Vernova Inc. is the NYSE-listed energy business spun out of General Electric in April 2024. It runs three segments: Power (gas turbines, nuclear services and reactor technology), Electrification (grid solutions, transformers, switchgear, power conversion and storage) and Wind. It is one of a very small number of firms that can supply both the generation asset and the grid equipment that connects it, which is why it is placed on three separate links of this chain.

exposure_summary.narrative: GE Vernova is the only issuer in this batch with three active placements: power-equipment (the money corner), energy-generation and grid-interconnect. That breadth is the exposure and also the caveat, because no single link's demand can be read off the consolidated numbers. The company's second-quarter 2026 release quantifies the data-centre pull directly for Electrification and separately describes gas turbine output capacity ramping through 2030, so both the equipment and the generation legs are disclosed rather than inferred.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: A data-centre revenue percentage is not disclosed. The second-quarter 2026 release (accession 0001996810-26-000147) does disclose a data-centre order figure for Electrification year to date, which is an order intake number, not a revenue share.
